speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiologic Neonatal Jaundice (Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia)

The progression of yellowing from the face to the trunk with scleral icterus is characteristic of this condition. While I am awaiting your total and direct bilirubin levels to confirm the severity, the clinical picture strongly suggests unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia rather than biliary atresia or sepsis.
